cards.ex: Can someone call the client back? — I'm on it.

cards.ko: (알람을) 잠깐 미루고 더 자다 / 빨리 적어 두다
cards.ex: I hit snooze three times. → Let me jot that down. (hit snooze = 알람 미루기, jot down = 메모하다)
Karaoke tonight? — Count me out, I'm too tired.
We haggled over the price. → I ditched my old phone. (haggle over N, ditch = 구어로 '버리다·빼먹다')
Want some more? — No thanks, I'm stuffed.

quiz.q: The printer's broken again. — Don't worry, I'm ___ it.
quiz.note: I'm on it = 제가 바로 할게요. 일을 맡을 때 짧고 자연스러운 대답.

quiz.q: My alarm went off, but I hit ___ and slept 10 more minutes.
quiz.note: hit snooze = 알람을 잠깐 미루다. snooze 자체로 '깜빡 졸다'라는 뜻도.
Count me out = 난 빠질래. 반대는 Count me in(나도 낄래).

quiz.q: At the market, my mom always tries to ___ over the price.

quiz.note: I'm stuffed = 배가 꽉 찼어요. stuffy는 '답답한, 코 막힌'이라 다른 뜻.

cards.ko: 잘 듣고 있어요, 어서 말해 봐요
cards.ex: I have some news. — Really? I'm all ears.

cards.ko: 눈치 있게 말하는, 요령 있는 / 잘 아는, 수완 좋은
cards.ex: She gave tactful feedback. → He's very tech-savvy. (tactful ↔ tactless, tech-savvy = 기계에 밝은)
It's so cold today. — You can say that again!
Don't fret about it. → I pondered the offer all night. (fret about N, ponder = 오래 따져 보다)

cards.ko: 오해하지 마세요 (좋게 말한 뒤 아쉬운 점 말할 때)
cards.ex: Don't get me wrong, I love my job. It's just really stressful.

quiz.q: So, what happened on your date? Tell me everything. I'm all ___ .
quiz.note: I'm all ears = 귀 쫑긋하고 듣고 있어. 이야기 재촉할 때.

quiz.q: My grandpa is surprisingly tech-___ . He even edits videos.
quiz.note: tech-savvy = 기계·IT에 밝은. money-savvy처럼 다른 말과도 붙어요.
You can say that again = 내 말이! 완전 공감할 때.

quiz.q: The exam is over. There's no point ___ about the results now.
quiz.note: fret (about N) = 끙끙 애태우다. worry보다 안절부절 느낌.

quiz.q: ___ , the hotel was nice. But the location was a problem.
quiz.note: Don't get me wrong = 오해 마. 칭찬 뒤에 '근데…' 붙일 때 써요.

cards.ex: Tickets sold out in an hour. If you didn't buy early, you missed the boat.
Winning once was a fluke. → That diet is just a fad. (a total fluke, a passing fad = 금방 지나갈 유행)
Who spilled the beans about the surprise party?
Don't gloat when you win. → Don't dwell on the past. (gloat over N, dwell on N = 계속 생각하다)
Everyone's buying that stock, but I'm not jumping on the bandwagon.

quiz.q: Prices went up 30% last month. I waited too long and ___ .
quiz.note: miss the boat = 좋은 기회를 놓치다. 과거면 missed the boat.

quiz.q: He's not really good at golf. That hole-in-one was a total ___ .
quiz.note: a fluke = 실력이 아니라 운. a total fluke로 자주.

quiz.q: Come on, ___ ! Who's the new manager?
quiz.note: spill the beans = 비밀을 불다. 재촉할 때 Spill the beans! 그대로 써요.

quiz.q: You made one mistake. Don't ___ on it. Just move on.
quiz.note: dwell on N = 지난 일을 자꾸 생각하다.

quiz.q: When the brand got popular, every celebrity ___ .
quiz.note: jump on the bandwagon = 남들 따라 대세에 올라타다.
